Definition: from G3319; a go-between, i.e. (simply) an internunciator, or (by implication) a reconciler (intercessor):--mediator.
BiblicalUsage: Mesites is a mediator, a go-between, one who stands between two parties and reconciles them. 1 Timothy 2:5 says there is one God, and one mediator between God and men, the man Christ Jesus, and Hebrews 8:6 says He is the mediator of a better covenant, established upon better promises. Galatians 3:19 says the law was ordained by angels in the hand of a mediator, and Galatians 3:20 adds that a mediator is not a mediator of one, but God is one.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe the mediator is the whole gospel in one word: God and men needed a go-between, and the go-between is a man. My position is that there is one mediator because there is one God, and no other name can stand in the middle.
